repos.title: Constraint Breeds Generalization: Temporal Dynamics as an Inductive Bias
repos.paper_summary: This paper argues that dissipative temporal dynamics, meaning phase-space contraction, act as an inductive bias that improves generalization in spiking neural networks (SNNs). Static features are converted into time series by a Duffing oscillator whose parameter δ sets the dynamics as expansive (δ<0), transition (δ≈0 to 2), or dissipative. Leaky integrate-and-fire neurons with leak β provide an architecture-level variant. On handwritten digits (64 features, 10 classes), SNNs trained in the transition regime generalize across a 12×12 matrix of encodings, while expansive-trained networks fail outside their training encoding. On CIFAR-10 patches, the transition regime yields localized, oriented receptive fields (structure score 0.206, versus 0.0541 for the best alternative in Table 1). Experiment 3 reports zero-shot transfer to unseen physical environments in reinforcement learning that beats baseline architectures. Limitations include fixed oscillator and fixed β parameters, and generality is checked only on a few alternative dynamical systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hypothesizes that dissipative temporal dynamics act as an inductive bias for generalization, tested at representational, structural, and behavioral levels.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Controls phase-space contraction through a single oscillator parameter δ for static inputs and neuron leak β for temporal inputs.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Argues the transition regime trades fit for stability; the authors flag fixed parameters and untested regime generality as limits.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Concludes that dissipative dynamics are an inductive bias, so generalization may depend on dynamical regime as much as on scale.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix lists oscillator equations and parameters, a dynamical indicator table, experiment details, Bayesian bound and gradient analyses, and extra figures.

repos.title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
repos.paper_summary:
Agensh is a multi-agent harness that coordinates concurrent LLM workers without a central orchestrator. Each worker executes an asynchronous loop: gathering context, claiming sub-tasks, taking action, verifying results, and merging progress into a shared workspace. Coordination relies on three infrastructure components: a Git-based shared workspace for code integration, a message interface for peer communication, and a shared context board for reusable findings.

The paper evaluates Agensh on the five hardest ProgramBench tasks using GPT-5.6-sol (high) with a 6-hour budget. Scaling from 1 to 128 agents increases the mean final test-pass rate from 19.31% to 28.78%, a 49% relative improvement. On the pandoc task, scaling to 1,024 agents raises the final test-pass rate from 33.89% to 55.06%. Larger organizations also reach comparable performance levels earlier; for instance, 128 agents exceed a 30% pass rate at 30 minutes, while single agents remain below this threshold for two hours. Limitations include reliance on specific underlying models and harnesses, and the need for staggered agent activation to manage scope contention in large-scale deployments.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Agensh replaces a central orchestrator with self-organized workers, and scaling 1 to 128 agents raises mean test-pass rate from 19.31% to 28.78%.

digest_headlines.heading: Multi-Agent Organization Harness
digest_headlines.headline: Each worker repeats a five-step loop over a shared workspace, message interface and shared context, with no central orchestrator.

digest_headlines.heading: Scaling Multi-Agent Organization to 1,024 Agents
digest_headlines.headline: Mean test-pass rate rises with 8, 32 and 128 agents, and pandoc reaches 55.06% with 1,024 agents.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior harnesses keep task assignment under a fixed lead or trained orchestrator, while some tools coordinate workers through shared state.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Agent count is proposed as a new scaling dimension, though every reported run uses one agent model.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix gives the worker prompt, the event-driven runtime, the experiment configuration and the staggered agent launch schedule.

repos.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
repos.paper_summary: Hy-Nomas is an 8B-parameter video world model that generates interactive video from free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple turns. It is built on HunyuanVideo 1.5 and generates variable-length segments conditioned on the current input and cached history. Its main design choice is action-aware causal attention: structured captions describe persistent scene and subject context that stays visible to later segments, while timestamped action instructions are limited to their own time window. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer converts user requests and interaction history into structured conditions for each next segment. Training follows a multi-stage curriculum (causal generation, text interaction, camera control, training on model-generated histories), then diffusion distillation. Human evaluation is reported as favoring Hy-Nomas over existing world models, but the text provided does not include the scores. The paper notes that temporal causality does not establish physical causality, that robotics adaptation is shown only as an initial LoRA demonstration, and that retrieving past views does not update off-screen state, such as a clock that should keep running. Weights, code, and benchmarks are released.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is an 8B interactive world model that follows free-form text and camera commands across multiple turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Data
digest_headlines.headline: Training videos are filtered, deduplicated, and annotated with camera trajectories and structured captions.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Architecture
digest_headlines.headline: Action-aware causal attention limits each action to its own time window, and camera tokens condition each segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Training Infrastructure
digest_headlines.headline: Sequence parallelism, compute-balanced packing and masked attention kernels support training on sequences up to 360K tokens.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Training
digest_headlines.headline: Training proceeds through causal, interaction and context curricula, then distillation from 100 to 4 steps per segment.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Inference
digest_headlines.headline: A vision-language Prompt Enhancer turns user requests into segment captions, and inference is optimized for a single device.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Human raters prefer Hy-Nomas over three interactive world models on most tasks, but Genie 3 leads on spatial memory.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Hy-Nomas is placed among video-based world models that add text and camera control to diffusion video generators.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion and Future Directions
digest_headlines.headline: Discussion names open challenges: response latency, action-grounded robotics, retrieval-based memory, and detailed caption quality.

digest_headlines.heading: Contributors
digest_headlines.headline: Contributors section lists core contributors, contributors, acknowledgments and leadership acknowledgments.

repos.title: TaoMate-HD: Progressive-Resolution Autoregressive Audio-Video Generation
repos.paper_summary: TaoMate-HD is an autoregressive model for streaming joint audio-video generation at 768×1376 resolution. Each chunk runs three denoising stages: two on a 480×864 grid and a final one on the 768×1376 grid. Each stage's clean prediction is encoded into a stage-specific key/value history bank for the same stage of the next chunk, so the next chunk can start before the previous one finishes refinement. Continuation training uses overlapping text windows and student-generated rollouts, scored by distribution-matching distillation. The model is a rank-128 LoRA trained on 10,000 distillation pairs over MiniMax-H3. On 100 self-constructed sequences of 1–10 minutes, progressive generation runs 1.60× faster than direct 768p generation (4.68 vs 2.93 FPS, serial). Stage-parallel deployment reaches 8.99 FPS, 1.92× the serial rate. Continuation training lowers character error rate from 30.75% to 19.57%. Limitations: the benchmark uses self-constructed sequences, the parallel configuration has slightly higher CER (21.28%), and serial TaoMate-HD's LipSync (7.061) trails MiniMax-H3 (7.569).

digest_headlines.heading: 1 Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: TaoMate-HD targets high-resolution audiovisual streaming, where dense denoising is costly and text updates can repeat or interrupt speech.

digest_headlines.heading: 2 Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work covers few-step distillation, progressive resolution, and stage-parallel inference, which uses history at stage output noise levels.

digest_headlines.heading: 3 Method
digest_headlines.headline: Chunks denoise in two low-resolution steps and one high-resolution step, with each stage's clean prediction reused as history.

digest_headlines.heading: 4 Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Serial TaoMate-HD scores highest on Temporal and AudioAes among streaming generators, reaching 0.913 and 4.407.

digest_headlines.heading: 5 Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion summarizes gains from progressive denoising and asymmetric distillation, extending to an hour of streaming.

repos.title: TaoMate-FVSR:Audio-Guided Facial Video Restoration
repos.paper_summary:
TaoMate-FVSR is an audio-guided facial video restoration framework for AI-generated video that also supports dubbing under replacement audio. It is a reference-guided flow model built on a Wan video DiT. Reconstruction starts from a mix of the source latent and Gaussian noise (strength 0.80 to 0.95), so the source mouth is not a fixed target. Reference frames and a four-frame motion history enter separate temporal slots. Training has two stages: visual restoration on degraded images and videos, then lip correction on degraded dubbed sources conditioned on target audio, with a SyncNet loss.

On a 150-video talking-head benchmark at 4× downsampling, it reports LPIPS 0.0793 and DISTS 0.0858, versus 0.1380 and 0.1421 for InstantRestore, and Sync-C/Sync-D of 7.413/7.561, versus 6.545/8.170 for SparkVSR. SparkVSR has higher PSNR (30.62 vs 28.67 dB) and SSIM (0.8863 vs 0.8836). On 30 replacement-audio clips, the enhanced-reference variant reaches Sync-C 8.175, versus 7.917 for the best cascade.

Limitations: the main comparison uses the ground-truth first frame as reference, and the enhanced-reference variant lowers PSNR to 23.52 dB. Native AIGC results are qualitative only.

digest_headlines.heading: 1 Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Restoring small AIGC faces requires lip and teeth detail that agrees with the spoken audio, not only sharper pixels.

digest_headlines.heading: 2 Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work spans facial and video restoration, generative restoration, visual dubbing, and audio-assisted restoration; the authors focus on unreliable mouths.

digest_headlines.heading: 3 Method
digest_headlines.headline: The method mixes source latents with noise to start flow reconstruction and injects sparse references and history into separate temporal slots.

digest_headlines.heading: 4 Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On the 150-video benchmark, Ours has the lowest paired perceptual error, while SparkVSR leads pixel-level fidelity.

digest_headlines.heading: 5 Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The authors state that reconstructed facial detail is a generative estimate, not evidence of true appearance, and raise impersonation risk.

repos.title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
repos.paper_summary: LMCache is an open-source library that extracts, stores, and transfers KV caches for LLM inference engines like vLLM and SGLang. It supports cross-query prefix caching and prefill-decode disaggregation by moving data between GPU memory, CPU DRAM, local disks, and remote storage. The system optimizes data movement using batched operations with configurable chunk sizes, layer-wise pipelining to overlap compute and I/O, and zero-copy mechanisms to minimize data duplication. A modular connector interface decouples LMCache from the evolving APIs of inference engines. In evaluations on H100 GPUs across six models, LMCache achieves up to 15× higher throughput and 2× lower latency compared to basic vLLM and commercial baselines. For prefill-decode disaggregation, it reduces mean time-to-first-token by 1.53–1.84× relative to native vLLM implementation. Limitations include reduced effectiveness at low network bandwidths; loading from remote storage only outperforms full prefill when input contexts exceed 256K tokens at 32 Gbps bandwidth. Additionally, context truncation in production environments can reduce prefix cache hit rates by half.

repos.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
repos.paper_summary:
TurnWise is a turn-level GRPO framework for streaming video RL that gives each response-or-wait decision its own advantage and weights decisions equally in the loss. For each trajectory, it scores every prefix with all later turns set to silence, subtracts the reward accrued before each turn, and normalizes the remaining return within the rollout group. Turn-mean aggregation averages token losses within each turn, then across turns, so output length does not set a turn's weight. No critic or extra rollouts are needed.

On Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TurnWise reaches 43.56 PAUC on ProactiveVQA, 21.59 Timing F1 on OVO-Timing, and 49.43 average accuracy on StreamingBench, which are 3.96, 3.87, and 0.69 points above the strongest non-TurnWise results. On Qwen3-VL-4B it reports 42.44, 11.15, and 58.96. Adding turn-mean aggregation to turn-level credit cuts repetition from 15.53 to 5.98 relative to credit-only training.

Limitations: experiments cover two Qwen backbones and three benchmarks, and the reward is the fixed PAUC-based scorer from MMDuet2. The alpha sweep tests only four correction strengths.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Shared trajectory-level advantages misassign credit to redundant replies and useful follow-ups in streaming video reinforcement learning.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior streaming video methods use trajectory-level GRPO, which broadcasts one advantage across all decision turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Methodology
digest_headlines.headline: Silence-completed prefix scores give each turn a remaining-return advantage, and turn-mean averaging weights every turn equally.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Experiments compare TurnWise with fine-tuned and reinforcement-learning baselines on three streaming benchmarks using two Qwen backbones.

digest_headlines.heading: Results and Discussions
digest_headlines.headline: TurnWise posts the best aggregate scores on all three benchmarks, reaching 43.56 on ProactiveVQA with the 3B backbone.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Turn-level credit without a critic supports higher-quality, better-timed and more selective streaming responses.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix derives the telescoping decomposition, the group-relative correction, the interpolation and warm-up schedule, and the dual-clipping loss.

repos.title: Reinforcement Learning for Versatile, Dynamic, and Robust Bipedal Locomotion Control
repos.paper_summary: This paper presents a dual-history reinforcement learning controller for bipedal robots, enabling diverse locomotion skills including walking, running, and jumping on the Cassie robot. The method uses a long-term input/output history encoder to adapt to dynamics changes and contact events, combined with a short-term history fed directly to the policy network to handle high-frequency control needs. Training follows a three-stage curriculum: single-task learning, task randomization, and dynamics randomization. In simulation ablations, the dual-history architecture outperforms baselines like RMA and state-feedback-only policies under randomized dynamics parameters. Real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, with the robot maintaining stable standing for 459 days, completing a 400-meter dash, and executing jumps up to 1.4 meters forward and 0.44 meters high. The authors identify task randomization as a key source of robustness distinct from dynamics randomization, promoting compliant recovery behaviors. Limitations include difficulty achieving precise velocity tracking during fast running and the requirement for specific reference motions; for instance, backward jumps could not be learned from a forward-jumping reference alone.

repos.title: Kornia: an Open Source Differentiable Computer Vision Library for PyTorch
repos.paper_summary: Kornia is an open-source PyTorch library implementing differentiable computer vision operators for GPU acceleration. The package structures algorithms into modules for color conversion, feature detection, filtering, and geometry, allowing users to embed classical vision tasks directly within neural networks for backpropagation. By using PyTorch's automatic differentiation, the library computes gradients for complex functions like image warping without manual derivative implementation. The authors benchmark Sobel edge detection on 256x256 RGB images using a GTX 1080 Ti, finding that Kornia achieves the best timing performance at large batch sizes on GPU, while CPU performance lags behind optimized libraries like OpenCV. Use cases include image registration via homography optimization and multi-view depth estimation from the SceneNet dataset. Limitations include the assumption of photometric consistency in depth estimation, which restricts accuracy to small view displacements, and the fact that adversarial perturbations demonstrated in feature matching examples are not imperceptible.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Kornia is presented as a PyTorch computer vision library that runs classical image operations on GPUs as differentiable modules.

digest_headlines.heading: Related work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior vision libraries are mostly CPU-based, and deep learning frameworks rely on them for pre- and post-processing.

digest_headlines.heading: Kornia: Computer Vision for PyTorch.
digest_headlines.headline: Kornia is organized into PyTorch-based submodules whose operators are differentiable, batched, device-agnostic and usable across distributed systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Use cases
digest_headlines.headline: Four use cases test the library on Sobel timing, homography registration, depth estimation and adversarial matching.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusions
digest_headlines.headline: Classical vision tasks are reported to solve easily in PyTorch with performance similar to existing libraries.

repos.title: StartLux-Decision: AutoThink Decision Models with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
repos.paper_summary: StartLux-Decision is a family of 0.8B–27B decision models that output probability distributions over candidate options for typed questions. The Instant variant makes one forward pass with bidirectional attention in its full-attention layers. The AutoThink variant first makes a one-pass prediction, then generates a reasoning trace of up to 4,096 tokens only when its top probability is below 0.9, and averages the initial and post-reasoning distributions. The final training stage adds reasoning supervision and RLCD2, which uses a frozen reference model, proper-score rewards, and a soft length penalty. RLCD2 raises the share of traces that finish within the generation limit by up to 48 percentage points and cuts average reasoning length by up to 65%, with accuracy largely preserved. On the public Decision Index 0.3 subset, Instant models beat the strongest comparable-scale open-weight decision models by 7.4–16.9 points, and the 27B AutoThink reaches 73.4. On DecisionPivot, a programmatically generated benchmark of contrast pairs, AutoThink beats its Instant counterpart by 11.5–18.4 points in pair accuracy. Policy-aware calibration reduces confidence–accuracy gaps to within 2.7 points across 184 settings. Stated limitations include generalization beyond represented task families and reliability under distribution shift, both left to future work.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Decision models need reasoning on hard cases without losing single-pass efficiency; the paper proposes two variants, RLCD2 training, and DecisionPivot.

digest_headlines.heading: Model Design and Training
digest_headlines.headline: Three-stage training gives Instant bidirectional attention and teaches AutoThink to reason only when its confidence is below 0.9.

digest_headlines.heading: RLCD2: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Deliberative Decisions
digest_headlines.headline: RLCD2 rewards reasoning by the change in proper score and penalizes traces beyond a soft budget.

digest_headlines.heading: Experimental Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: On the public Decision Index 0.3 subset, Instant models lead comparable-scale references by 7.4–16.9 points.

digest_headlines.heading: Capability and Reliability Analysis
digest_headlines.headline: Selecting among candidates makes reported confidence overconfident, and policy-aware calibration narrows the gaps across 184 settings.

digest_headlines.heading: Efficient Inference and Deployment
digest_headlines.headline: Single-pass Instant readouts on a single GPU take 24–52 ms for 256-token prompts and 31–98 ms for 1,024-token prompts.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Future work targets generalization beyond represented task families and reliability under distribution shift.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix documents training data sources and decontamination, policy-aware calibration proofs, and serving configuration safeguards.
